articleBody:
- [ ] Attic inspection record — Confirms whether your target wall supports roof trusses or ceiling joists before demo starts.
- [ ] Electrical circuit inventory — Identifies how many switches, outlets, and feed lines run through the wall and require relocation.
- [ ] Plumbing and vent stack verification — Determines if water supply pipes, drain lines, or plumbing vents must be moved into the floor or adjacent walls.
- [ ] HVAC register and return check — Verifies whether heating and cooling ducts pass through the partition and need rerouting to balance air circulation.
- [ ] Flooring transition evaluation — Identifies whether existing flooring runs under the wall or if you must patch and replace flooring across adjoining rooms.
- [ ] Range hood venting path — Confirms you have a clear route to vent cooking grease and odors directly outside once the wall is gone.
- [ ] Island clearance measurement — Verifies you maintain 42 to 48 inches of walkway between your planned island and living room furniture.
- [ ] Local permit requirements check — Confirms what plans and trade permits your local building department requires before structural demolition begins.
- [ ] Written scope and allowance document — Clarifies contractor responsibilities for structural beams, drywall finishing, and final inspections.

How to use this checklist:
Work through these items with your contractor during your initial home walkthrough. Having answers to each point prevents costly surprise change orders once walls are opened up.
